<think>
Use the law of cosines for each angle, naming angles by their opposite sides.

Opposite 2, the cosine is [6+(1+√3)²−4]/[2√6(1+√3)]=(6+2√3)/[2√6(1+√3)]=1/√2. This angle is 45°.

Opposite √6, the cosine is [4+(1+√3)²−6]/[4(1+√3)]=(2+2√3)/[4(1+√3)]=1/2. This angle is 60°.

Opposite 1+√3, the cosine is [4+6−(1+√3)²]/(4√6)=(3−√3)/(2√6)=(√6−√2)/4. This angle is 75°.

Thus the three angles are 45°, 60°, and 75°.

Final Answer: 45, 60, 75

<think>

The first component is 1·4−(−2)(−3)=−2.

The second component is (−2)·1−3·4=−14.

The third component is 3(−3)−1·1=−10.

Final Answer: 10√3

We can determine the sum using the tangent addition formula and the acute-angle restrictions.

Since tan θ=1/7 and θ is acute, θ=arctan(1/7), so 0<θ<π/4.

<think>
For a subset of size k, all entries lie in {k,…,15}. If its ordered entries are a₁<…<aₖ, set bⱼ=aⱼ−(j−1). The no-consecutive condition makes the bⱼ distinct increasing entries of {k,…,16−k}, a set of 17−2k entries. Thus the count is C(17−2k,k), and feasibility requires k≤5.

For k=1, the count is C(15,1)=15.

For k=2, the count is C(13,2)=78.

For k=3, the count is C(11,3)=165.

For k=4, the count is C(9,4)=126.

For k=5, the count is C(7,5)=21.

These disjoint nonempty cases total 15+78+165+126+21=405.
</think>
Final Answer: 405

<think>
There are 21 dots altogether. Removing a dot changes the parity of exactly one face, and each face is equally likely to be rolled.

The even faces contain 2+4+6=12 dots. With probability 12/21, removal makes an even face odd, leaving four odd faces. This case contributes (12/21)(4/6)=8/21.

The odd faces contain 1+3+5=9 dots. With probability 9/21, removal makes an odd face even, leaving two odd faces. This case contributes (9/21)(2/6)=3/21.

The probability is 8/21+3/21=11/21.
</think>
Final Answer: 11/21

<think>
There are C(25,5)=53130 equally likely committees. Failure means an all-boy or all-girl committee, two disjoint cases.

An all-boy committee has C(10,5)=252 possible choices.

An all-girl committee has C(15,5)=3003 possible choices.

The desired probability is 1−(252+3003)/53130=475/506.
</think>
Final Answer: 475/506

<think>
Partition attendance by the weather, using the forecast probability and the corresponding conditional attendance probability.

Rain and attendance have joint probability 0.40·0.20=0.08.

Sunny weather and attendance have joint probability (1−0.40)·0.80=0.48.

Attendance therefore has probability 0.08+0.48=0.56, or 56%.
</think>
Final Answer: 56%

<think>
All 6⁴=1296 ordered rolls are equally likely. Count favorable rolls by their number of ones; each remaining face other than 1 or 6 has four choices.

Exactly one 1 requires zero 6s: C(4,1)4³=256 rolls.

Exactly two 1s permit zero or one 6: C(4,2)4²+ C(4,2)C(2,1)4=96+48=144 rolls.

Exactly three 1s permit zero or one 6: C(4,3)4+C(4,3)=16+4=20 rolls.

Exactly four 1s give one roll.

The probability is (256+144+20+1)/1296=421/1296.
</think>
Final Answer: 421/1296

<think>
List perfect powers up to 150, then take the complement. Positive values from negative bases have even exponents and are already squares. The value 1 is included because 1=1².

Squares have bases 1 through 12: {1,4,9,16,25,36,49,64,81,100,121,144}, giving 12 values.

Cubes have positive bases 1 through 5: {1,8,27,64,125}. Their values outside the square list are {8,27,125}.

Fourth and sixth powers are squares. Fifth powers have bases 1 and 2, giving {1,32}; seventh powers have bases 1 and 2, giving {1,128}. Every exponent at least 8 with absolute base at least 2 exceeds 150, since 2⁸=256.

The union has 12+3+1+1=17 values. Thus 150−17=133 numbers are not perfect powers, with probability 133/150.
</think>
Final Answer: 133/150

<think>
A Cubs series win ends on its fourth victory. For a series lasting n games, the first n−1 games contain three Cubs wins, and the last game is a Cubs win. Each game has win probability 3/5 and loss probability 2/5.

Winning in four games has probability (3/5)⁴=81/625.

Winning in five games has probability C(4,3)(3/5)⁴(2/5)=648/3125.

Winning in six games has probability C(5,3)(3/5)⁴(2/5)²=648/3125.

Winning in seven games has probability C(6,3)(3/5)⁴(2/5)³=2592/15625.

These disjoint cases sum to 11097/15625=0.710208, or 71.0208%. Rounded to the nearest whole percent, this is 71%.
</think>
Final Answer: 71%
